The 1st axis is dropped. x_sum_dropped <- rray_remove_axes(rray_sum(x, axes = 1), axes = 1) x_sum_dropped #> [1]  6 15  # Now broadcasting doesn't work! rray_divide(x, x_sum_dropped) #> Error in `rray_divide()`: #> ! Can't find common dimensions at axis 1. `x` has dimension 3 and `y` has dimension 2.  # So you have to add back the axis manually # (NumPy has slightly cleaner ways to do this, but it's still an extra step) x_sum_reshaped <- rray_insert_axes(x_sum_dropped, axes = 1) rray_divide(x, x_sum_reshaped) #>           [,1]      [,2] #> [1,] 0.1666667 0.2666667 #> [2,] 0.3333333 0.3333333 #> [3,] 0.5000000 0.4000000

title: Roll an array — rray-roll
code: # Positive `n` moves elements toward the end rray_roll(1:5, n = 2, axes = 1) #> [1] 4 5 1 2 3  # Negative `n` moves them toward the start rray_roll(1:5, n = -1, axes = 1) #> [1] 2 3 4 5 1  # Large `n` circles around rray_roll(1:5, n = 7, axes = 1) #> [1] 4 5 1 2 3  x <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2, dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2"), c("a", "b", "c")))  # Roll the columns, names move with the data rray_roll(x, n = 1, axes = 2) #>    c a b #> r1 5 1 3 #> r2 6 2 4  # Roll the rows rray_roll(x, n = 1, axes = 1) #>    a b c #> r2 2 4 6 #> r1 1 3 5  # Roll both axes by the same `n` rray_roll(x, n = 1, axes = c(1, 2)) #>    c a b #> r2 6 2 4 #> r1 5 1 3  # Or by one `n` per axis rray_roll(x, n = c(1, -1), axes = c(1, 2)) #>    b c a #> r2 4 6 2 #> r1 3 5 1  y <- matrix(1:12, nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)  # Roll each row by its own `n`, given as a one column matrix rray_roll_each(y, n = matrix(c(1, 0, -1), ncol = 1), axis = 2) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] #> [1,]    4    1    2    3 #> [2,]    5    6    7    8 #> [3,]   10   11   12    9  # Roll each column by its own `n`, given as a one row matrix rray_roll_each(y, n = matrix(c(0, 1, 2, 3), nrow = 1), axis = 1) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] #> [1,]    1   10    7    4 #> [2,]    5    2   11    8 #> [3,]    9    6    3   12  # Names on `axis` are dropped, since no single name fits each position rray_roll_each(x, n = matrix(c(1, 2), ncol = 1), axis = 2) #>    [,1] [,2] [,3] #> r1    5    1    3 #> r2    4    6    2
